author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

text:
I built my own 8086 in SystemVerilog from scratch

DOS boots up fine, some old games runs very slow, much slower than a real IBM PC.

I have a web front end hooks up to a xezim simulator backend

https://lnkd.in/gTMXAuZ7

author.name: Bondan Rufen
author.headline: Co-Founder | SystemVerilog, SystemC | Xezim Creator / Maintainer

comments.text: Wow..Great effort. DOS is like dinosaur, it becomes fossilized. It reminds me when running DOS 1.0 functions for X86 compliance tests.

author.name: Horace Chan
author.headline: Expert in applying AI in verification

replies.text:
Bondan Rufen AI did all the hard work, I just keep yelling at it to make it work harder.

Now, with a 8086 running in simulator, I move on to another crazy stupid idea, rewrite DOS in Rust.

author.name: Bondan Rufen
author.headline: Co-Founder | SystemVerilog, SystemC | Xezim Creator / Maintainer

replies.text: Horace Chan X86 and DOS were really two sides of the same coin, each helped make the other successful.
